summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style code that downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time, extracts and chmod+x's the bun binary, then execFileSync-runs the sibling math_init.js under that alien runtime. math_init.js is a 727 KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, rotated string-array `n7gIxM`/`WV8StW`, hex-mangled identifiers) whose filename bears no relation to a React SDK, and whose content is not reviewable prior to execution. The package identifies itself as `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` but its description, README title, and install instructions all reference `@verdocs/web-sdk-react` (the legitimate Verdocs Web SDK), so the differently-scoped clone functions as a brand-impersonating lure that delivers the preinstall dropper. On `npm install`, arbitrary author-controlled code executes on the installer's machine via a freshly-downloaded second-language runtime chosen to bypass Node-focused scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
